sources.entry: Build Your First Streamlit Data App

summary.title: Create an app - Streamlit Docs
summary.one_liner: You learn to build an interactive Streamlit data app that loads, caches, charts, maps, and filters a public NYC Uber pickup dataset.
keywords: how to filter data with a slider in streamlit
how to cache data in python web app
deploy streamlit app to community cloud
takeaways: Write a Python script with Streamlit, add a title, and run it with `streamlit run`, which reloads the app as you save changes.
Use @st.cache_data on a data-loading function so Streamlit reuses cached results when the function's inputs and code are unchanged.
Draw a histogram with NumPy and st.bar_chart, and plot geographic points with st.map.
Add interactive widgets such as st.slider and st.checkbox to filter the data and show or hide sections of the app.
Deploy a public GitHub-hosted app for free on Streamlit Community Cloud.
summary.summary: This tutorial walks through building a Streamlit app that explores a public Uber pickups dataset for New York City. It proceeds step by step: loading CSV data with pandas, caching the loader with @st.cache_data, showing raw data, drawing an hourly histogram with st.bar_chart, plotting pickups on a map with st.map, and filtering by hour using a slider and a show/hide checkbox. It explains how caching checks inputs and function code, along with its limitations, and ends with the full script and steps to deploy on Streamlit Community Cloud.
